title: Trieu Tien Episode 17: The Battle at the Moon Gate
audience: Fans of Chinese fantasy, wuxia/xianxia drama viewers, 18-35 demographic who enjoy epic visual storytelling
tone: Heroic, melancholic, epic, cinematic, emotionally charged

concept.hook: They met at the moon gate where they used to train together — now enemies with blades drawn.
concept.story_arc: Moon Gate approached → Past floods back → Training ground remembered → Battle erupts → Neither can strike
concept.emotion: Nostalgia → Longing → Memory clash → Battle intensity → Impossible deadlock

shots.prompt: Wide establishing at full moon — the Moon Gate stands in a mountain clearing, ancient white stone glowing silver under the moon. The same gate where they trained as teenagers. She arrives first. She runs her fingers along the stone arch — and sees their names carved into the inside: Trieu Tien + [his birth name], carved with a sword thirty years ago. Camera: wide, full moon, glowing Moon Gate, her fingers on carved names, thirty years of history in stone. 6 seconds.
shots.camera: Wide — full moon, glowing Moon Gate, carved names 'Trieu Tien + his name', fingers on stone, 6s
shots.narration: He had carved their names into the Moon Gate the night before he left for the war. She had laughed and told him the moon would witness it forever. And the moon had. Through everything.
shots.sfx: Moonlight settling, stone cool against skin, wind through gate, bittersweet strings

shots.prompt: Memory montage close-up — rapid cuts: a teenage boy teaching a teenage girl the third sword form; him catching her when she falls during practice; them eating dumplings under the gate at midnight; him swearing on the moon that he will return; her pressing her thumbprint into wet clay beside his name. Camera: rapid memory montage, warm golden tones, joy and first love. 6 seconds.
shots.camera: Memory montage — teaching sword form, catching her fall, dumplings at midnight, oath on moon, thumbprint in clay, 6s
shots.narration: Before titles, before war, before empire — they were just two children under the moon gate. And every technique she knew, she had learned from him.
shots.sfx: Young laughter, soft wind, sword form whoosh, moon oath whisper, memory swell

shots.prompt: Close-up — he arrives. He stops at the gate's opposite side. They face each other across the arch. The same moon above. The same carved names above them. Neither draws. He speaks first: 'I kept my oath.' 'You burned the temple.' 'I kept my oath.' She draws the Crimson Blade. He draws his general's sword. The blades meet at the center of the gate — exactly where they once practiced together. Camera: close-up, both blades drawn, meeting at Moon Gate center, thirty years collapsing into one strike. 6 seconds.
shots.camera: Close-up — both blades drawn, meeting at Moon Gate center, 'I kept my oath', thirty years in one strike, 6s
shots.narration: I kept my oath. Three words. And every night he had spent believing she hated him — he had kept it. Not to her forgiveness. Not to her love. Just to the promise he made to the moon.
shots.sfx: Blades meeting, metal singing, his quiet voice, her sharp breath, moonlight intensifying

shots.prompt: Wide cinematic — they BATTLE. But it is not war — it is a dance. Every move is a memory. She attacks with the third form — the one he taught her. He parries with the counter her father taught HIM. Each exchange is a conversation between their pasts. Cherry blossoms fall from ancient trees overhead. It is the most beautiful fight she has ever fought. Camera: wide, battle-as-dance, every move referencing a memory, falling cherry blossoms, moonlit beauty. 6 seconds.
shots.camera: Wide — battle as dance, every move referencing past training, cherry blossoms falling, moonlit beauty, 6s
shots.narration: She realized it then: she was not fighting to kill him. She was fighting to feel him again. Every technique was a memory. Every parry was a conversation. They had never been more honest with each other than in this moonlight.
shots.sfx: Blade duet singing, cherry blossoms landing, soft battle cry, epic beautiful strings

shots.prompt: Extreme close-up — she drives the Crimson Blade toward his heart. He does not dodge. He lowers his sword. She STOPS the blade one inch from his chest — her hand shaking. She cannot do it. She lowers the blade. He catches her as she staggers. They stand together under the carved names. 'I cannot kill you,' she says. 'I know,' he says. Camera: extreme close-up, blade stopped one inch from heart, lowered, him catching her, both defeated by love. 6 seconds.
shots.camera: Extreme close-up — blade stopped one inch from heart, she lowers it, he catches her, 'I cannot kill you', 6s
shots.narration: She could not kill him. And he had known — had always known — that she would not. That was why he had come here. Not to fight. To give her the chance to do what he could never ask her to do.
shots.sfx: Blade stopping, her shaking breath, his arms catching her, their breathing synchronized, cherry blossom settling, emotional release

audio.narration: He had carved their names into the Moon Gate the night before he left for the war. She had laughed and told him the moon would witness it forever. And the moon had. Through everything. Before titles, before war, before empire — they were just two children under the moon gate. And every technique she knew, she had learned from him. I kept my oath. Three words. And every night he had spent believing she hated him — he had kept it. Not to her forgiveness. Not to her love. Just to the promise he made to the moon. She realized it then: she was not fighting to kill him. She was fighting to feel him again. Every technique was a memory. Every parry was a conversation. They had never been more honest with each other than in this moonlight. She could not kill him. And he had known — had always known — that she would not. That was why he had come here. Not to fight. To give her the chance to do what he could never ask her to do.
audio.bg_music: Beautiful Chinese battle orchestral, moon gate theme, blade dance, cherry blossoms, love and war merged 80 BPM
